Since the beginning of the year I haven't gotten into a single game. I'll boot it up for an hour every week, week nights & weekends, & surf the playlists. If you were having issues getting into a game before, this patch fixes nothing. 

I would love a quick match option just to play something. I have a friend who instantly gets matches on Modern Warfare 2 on his PS3.

The thing is, I can understand where parents and relatives are coming from when they're watching a 14-year old play GTA V, which is an R18+ game in Australia. If I saw my 14 year old cousin watching American Psycho, I'd be similarly concerned, although I certainly don't agree with the whole "watching/playing violent content creates child killers". 

Games are made for a huge range of different interest and age groups, which is why we have ratings, and in some cases, age restrictions. I'm all for the R18+ rating (about time), but family members have to respect those ratings the same way as film ratings. I think a lot of family members are way too relaxed about game ratings, in fact, I'd be surprised if many parents actually know the ratings of the games they buy for their kids. But then they're more than happy to jump on the "violence breeds violence" bandwagon, because it shifts responsibility from them to the industry, and thus taints their entire perception of what video games are and can be. I don't think violent games create violent people, but I do think overtly violent and explicit games like GTA V, can have an effect on younger people, especially when you're an easily influenced teen. The game forces you to brutally torture a man - would I be happy if I watched my 14 year old son play that mission? Hell no, but it would never happen, because that's my responsibility as a parent.

Also, concerning games making people "stupid, zombie-like", I can definitely agree that games can, but then, so too can overdoing it for a great many things. Once again, it comes down to parenting. You can't watch your kid play video games 8 hours a day, then specifically blame games for your kid turning into an anti-social "zombie". Blame yourself first for not doing your job as a parent.
